title: Blockification of <legend>
body:
https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-fieldset-and-legend-elements says:

> A fieldset element's rendered legend, if any, is expected to act as follows:
> * The 'display' property is expected to behave as if its computed value was blockified.
> > Note: This does not change the computed value.

However, browsers do not behave like that. Blink in particular, blockifies legends at computed-value time, and it blockifies all legends, regardless of whether you're the rendered legend. This allows them to support arbitrary `display` values in the legend much more easily.

(Test-case: `data:text/html,A<legend style="display: inline"></legend>B`. Chromium has https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=883541 to track this spec divergence)

@MatsPalmgren was recently doing some work in Gecko to make the legend support various `display` types like `grid`, `flex`, etc, and implementing the spec to the letter is unnecessarily complicated / special-casey, IMHO.

Given that:

 * Most (all?) other blockifications happen at computed value time (see `position: absolute` or `float`s).
 * Treating _only_ the rendered legend specially at computed-value time is error-prone / complicated (because it requires detecting whether the fieldset would have a box, and whether it'd be the right kind of box, and whether you're a rendered legend basically depends on your style, which in the general case is circular).
 * Blockifying at used value time while supporting arbitrary display values is also unnecessarily complicated, more-so if we limit this to the rendered legend.
 * Multiple legends in a fieldset, or legends outside of a fieldset are kind of an edge case.
 * The Chromium behavior seems web-compatible, and (I think) unlikely to change (because it is a simpler implementation).

I think it'd be better if the HTML spec was changed to say that all legends are blockified at computed-value time, much like all absolutely-positioned elements are blockified at computed-value time, etc.

Would that make sense?

cc: @MatsPalmgren @zcorpan @mstensho
